first: अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः ।
en: Krishna said: One who does the work that should be done without depending on its results is a renouncer and a yogi, not one who merely gives up the sacred fire and all rites.

first: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव ।
en: Pandava, know that what people call renunciation is yoga. No one becomes a yogi without giving up selfish plans.
For the sage who wants to climb to yoga, action is said to be the means. For one who has climbed to yoga, calm is said to be the means.
When a person is not attached to sense objects or to actions, and has given up all selfish plans, that person is said to have climbed to yoga.
Lift yourself up by your own self; do not let yourself sink. The self alone is one's own friend, and the self alone is one's own enemy.
The self is a friend to one who has conquered himself by the self. But for one who has not, the self acts like an enemy.
For one who has conquered himself and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
A yogi who is satisfied with knowledge and wisdom, firm as a rock, master of the senses, and who sees a lump of earth, a stone and gold as the same, is called steady.
One who looks equally on well-wishers, friends, enemies, neutral people, those in between, the hateful, relatives, the good and the wicked, stands out.
A yogi should always keep the mind steady, staying alone in a quiet place, with mind and body controlled, without hopes and without wanting to own things.
In a clean place he should set up a firm seat for himself, neither too high nor too low, covered with kusha grass, a deerskin and a cloth, one over the other.
Sitting there, making the mind one-pointed, and controlling the work of thought and the senses, he should practise yoga to purify himself.
Holding the body, head and neck straight and still, steady, he should look at the tip of his nose without looking around.
Calm and fearless, firm in the vow of self-restraint, with the mind controlled and thinking of me, he should sit steady with me as his highest goal.
Always keeping himself steady in this way, the yogi with a controlled mind reaches the peace that rests in me and ends in freedom.
Arjuna, yoga is not for one who eats too much or for one who does not eat at all, nor for one who sleeps too much or for one who stays awake too much.
For one who is moderate in food and rest, moderate in effort at work, and moderate in sleep and waking, yoga takes away all sorrow.
When the controlled mind rests in the self alone, free from longing for any desire, a person is then called steady in yoga.

first: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
en: "Like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker": this is the picture used for a yogi whose mind is controlled and who practises yoga of the self.
When the mind, held back by the practice of yoga, comes to rest, and when, seeing the self by the self, one is content in the self;
when one knows that endless joy which is grasped by the intellect and lies beyond the senses, and resting there one never moves from the truth;

first: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः ।
en: having gained which one thinks no other gain is greater, and resting in which one is not shaken even by great sorrow;
know that this breaking of the link with sorrow is called yoga. This yoga should be practised firmly, with an undiscouraged mind.
Giving up completely all desires born of selfish plans, and holding back the whole group of senses on every side with the mind;
one should little by little become still, with the intellect held by firmness. Fixing the mind in the self, one should think of nothing else.
Wherever the restless and unsteady mind wanders, one should hold it back from there and bring it under the control of the self.
Supreme joy comes to this yogi whose mind is at peace, whose passion is calmed, who has become Brahman and is free from sin.
Always keeping himself steady in this way, the yogi free from sin easily enjoys the endless joy of contact with Brahman.
One who is steady in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self. Such a person sees the same everywhere.

first: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति ।
en: One who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me, I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to me.
The yogi who, established in oneness, worships me as living in all beings, lives in me, however he may live.
Arjuna, the yogi who, by comparing with himself, sees the same everywhere, in pleasure or in pain, is thought to be the highest.
Arjuna said: Madhusudana, I do not see how this yoga of sameness that you have taught can last, because the mind is restless.

first: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्‌दृढम् ।
en: For the mind is restless, Krishna, unruly, strong and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold back as the wind.
Krishna said: No doubt, mighty-armed one, the mind is hard to control and restless. But, son of Kunti, it is held back by practice and by letting go of desire.

first: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः ।
en: I agree that yoga is hard to reach for one who has not mastered himself. But one who has mastered himself and keeps trying can reach it by the right means.
Arjuna said: Krishna, what end comes to one who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind slips away from yoga before reaching its goal?
Mighty-armed one, falling from both, does he not perish like a broken cloud, without support and confused on the path to Brahman?
Krishna, please remove this doubt of mine completely. There is no one but you who can remove it.
Krishna said: Son of Pritha, there is no ruin for him either in this world or the next. My friend, no one who does good ever comes to a bad end.
One who has fallen from yoga reaches the worlds of those who did good deeds and lives there for very many years. Then he is born in a home of pure and well-off people.
Or he is born in a family of wise yogis. Such a birth is very hard to get in this world.
There he regains the understanding he had in his earlier body, and from there he strives again for perfection, joy of the Kurus.
By that earlier practice he is carried forward even without wanting it. Even one who only wishes to know yoga goes beyond the ritual words of the Veda.
But the yogi who strives with effort, cleansed of sin and perfected over many births, then reaches the highest goal.
The yogi is greater than those who practise austerity, greater even than the learned, and greater than those who perform rites. So be a yogi, Arjuna.
And of all yogis, the one who worships me with faith, with his inner self absorbed in me, I consider the most steady in yoga.
